In 1929 Harry Hare, the first Belgrave President ever of the S.T.C.C.A., handed to his club mates the DEWAR Shield for winning the Championship (for the first time), and the six team winners medals to:- BILL MITCHELL (4), ARTHUR PENNY (7), ARTHUR ALLUM (12), BILL WEBB (16), PAUL KHLOPIN (23) and ALEC ROBERTSHAW (26).
Going back to the 1934 London - Brighton Walk, one of the members of the winning Belgrave team was Paul Khlopin, a Russian. Formerly a cross country runner he took to walking.
Paul Khlopin who left Russian after World War I was a cross-country runner who later became a long-distance walker and figured in our London - Brighton teams.

On race day at Belgrave Hall he caught the smell of liniment from the dressing room and recounted how Paul Khlopin, a Belgravian who came from Russia at the end of the first World War, used to anoint himself with a mixture of olive oil, wintergreen and vinegar.
